battle.name: 汴京之戰
battle.brief: 一二三二年正月，蒙古睿宗拖雷部與速不台騎兵合圍金國南京汴京，同時金國十五萬北援大軍在鈞州三峰山被殲，援兵斷絕。金廷倚內外兩重城垣死守，蒙古軍在城外發砲、穴地、填壕，圍城約四月，軍糧告罄而城破，哀宗出奔歸德。配重投石車壓制城頭、封鎖援道，工程與糧秣先於刀兵決定了這場城下的勝負。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 交戰的兩方是蒙古帝國與金朝。蒙古一方，一二三一年秋大汗窩闊台分三路大舉攻金：睿宗拖雷領東路，一二三一年八月強攻大散關、鳳州、饒鳳關，其後假道漢水取唐州、鄧州，兵鋒直指汴京；木木哥領西路取關中，卻自一二三一年末起被阻於鳳翔城下，直到一二三二年秋天才攻下此城；速不台等領河北方向的輕騎，取真定、中山一線南下，與拖雷會師。真正完成合圍的，是拖雷的東路與速不台部，外加沿途收編的漢地降軍與徵發的匠人。蒙古軍骨幹是草原騎射，編制以十進制為單位，圍城時另編工匠隊、投石手隊與填壕步卒，漢地砲手與攻城工匠被編入攻城序列，軍中亦隨有來自西域的砲手。另一方的金朝，南京汴京是宣宗遷都後的都城，朝廷以尚書省、樞密院分掌政與軍，京畿由禁軍、漢地簽軍及御林、護衛各軍組成，守城由汴京留守完顏合剌與統軍司節制，兵源與財賦大半靠臨時括取河南、河北，鎧甲與攻城器械多臨時修造。南宋不在交戰名單上，卻是被爭奪的第三方：蒙古借道被拒，一二三三年宋將孟珙收復襄陽、樊城，一二三四年與蒙古軍會師攻破蔡州。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Mongol Empire and the Jin dynasty. On the Mongol side, in the autumn of 1231 the Great Khan Ogedei split the invasion of Jin into three columns: Tolui, the Regent, took the eastern route, forcing Dasan Pass, Fengzhou and Raofeng Pass in August and November 1231 and then moving down the Han River to seize Tangzhou and Dengzhou, pointing straight at Bianjing; Mongke led the western column into the Guanzhong basin but was held up before Fengxiang from the end of 1231 and did not take that city until the autumn of 1232; Subutai led light horse through Hebei, taking the line of Zhending and Zhongshan and moving south to join Tolui. The force that actually closed the ring around Bianjing was therefore Tolui's eastern column together with Subutai's men, supplemented by Han Chinese troops recruited from the surrendered population and by craftsmen conscripted along the line of march. The backbone of the Mongol army was the steppe archer, organised on the decimal system, but for the siege they formed separate corps of engineers, of stone-throwers and of sappers for filling the ditch, and Han Chinese artillerymen and siege craftsmen were enrolled into the assault columns, with artillerists from the western regions also serving in the camp. On the Jin side, Nanjing, the capital to which Xuanzong had moved the court in 1214, was administered by the Department of State Affairs and the Privy Council, with the capital's garrison drawn from the imperial guards, the locally levied Han Chinese militia and the Imperial and Guard armies, and the defence of the city directed by the Nanjing commander Wanyan Hela and the Military Command Office. Men, money and equipment were raised by hurried levies in Henan and Hebei, and much of the armour and siege ordnance was made up on the spot. The Southern Song was not a party to the battle but the prize both sides were bargaining over: the Mongols were refused passage, Meng Gong of Song recovered Xiangyang and Fancheng in 1233, and in 1234 Song and Mongol armies struck Caizhou together.
people: 金哀宗完顏守緒是這一局的中心人物。一二一四年宣宗把都城從中都遷到汴京，到一二三二年這位天子手上能守的只剩四面城牆：同年正月，拖雷部與速不台部會師，十五萬北援大軍在鈞州三峰山被殲，援兵斷絕，哀宗只能在城內坐等。汴京留守完顏合剌主持城防，城破之前自盡殉城；金廷在圍城之中屢次遣使出城，或求援或乞和，皆無回音。完顏合達與移剌蒲阿是正月出城的兩位主帥，一個戰死、一個被擒不降，等於把汴京最後一點指望提前葬送；完顏陳和尚在鈞州城破後親至敵營拒降而死，成為金末守將的寫照；武仙則收攏十萬潰兵屯於鄧州留山、威遠寨，奉詔回援汴京卻遲遲不能解圍，翌年被宋將孟珙擊潰。蒙古方面的決策層是窩闊台、拖雷與木木哥：窩闊台坐鎮中軍策應，拖雷在唐、鄧一線游弋並選定截擊的時機與地點，木木哥受阻鳳翔使東西兩路無法會合；速不台率河北方向的騎兵直抵城下，攻城與追擊都由他這一路推動。蒙古的砲手與隨軍工匠在《元史》裏多不具名，只以西域人與匠戶出現，卻是把城牆壓到不能抬頭的那批人。
peopleEn: Emperor Aizong of Jin, Wanyan Shouxu, stood at the centre of this scene. Xuanzong had moved the capital from Zhongdu to Bianjing in 1214, and by 1232 this emperor had nothing left to hold but four walls. In the first month of that year Tolui's and Subutai's columns joined forces and the relief host of 150,000 was annihilated at Mount Three Peaks near Jinzhou; the road to help was cut, and Aizong could only wait inside the city. Wanyan Hela, the Nanjing commander, directed the defence and killed himself before the city fell; the court sent envoys out of the city more than once, to ask for help or for terms, and received no answer. Wanyan Heda and Yelü Pua, the two commanders of the relief army that marched out in the first month, were killed in action or captured and refused to submit, and in effect buried the last hope of Bianjing before the siege had properly begun. Wanyan Chenheshang, who was killed after going to the enemy camp to refuse surrender, became the emblem of the Jin officer who would not live; Wuxian gathered a hundred thousand routed men at Liushan and Weiyuan stockade near Dengzhou, was ordered to relieve Bianjing and never reached the city, and was beaten the following year by Meng Gong of Song. On the Mongol side the decisions belonged to Ogedei, Tolui and Mongke: the Great Khan sat in the centre directing the campaign, Tolui loitered along the Tangzhou and Dengzhou line until he could choose both the ground and the hour of the interception, and Mongke's stalemate before Fengxiang kept the eastern and western columns from ever joining. Subutai's horse came down through Hebei to the foot of the walls, and both the siege and the pursuit were carried by that column. The Mongols' artillerymen and engineers are mostly nameless in the Yuan records, appearing only as men from the western regions and as artisan households, yet they were the ones who pressed the defenders down behind the parapet.
kits: 本卡是配重投石車，歐洲十二世紀初約一一〇〇年前後的形制：長臂末端懸著石塊或填土的木箱作配重，靠槓桿把石彈甩過城牆。射程可達數百步，遠超弓弩，可以越牆打進城內，也可以打擊牆後的人馬與器械；代價是它笨重、裝填慢、精度低，必須預先平整基座、拉緊繩索並備足人力，一旦被壓制或遇襲就難以轉移。與之對照的是中國同期以人力槓桿運作的拋石車（砲車）：構造簡單、機動性好，但射程與投射力不及配重式。配重式的巨砲是十二世紀末至十三世紀初隨西域技術東傳而來，《元史》中正式留下名號的是一二三四年蔡州之戰的回回砲，其發石重逾百斤，響如雷霆；而一二三二年汴京之戰的攻城大軍已帶有西域砲手與巨型石砲，《金史》《元史》的圍城記載裡有穴地與發砲的字樣。攻城序列中還有撞車、飛梯、攻城塔、填壕用的板橋與柴土，並封鎖汴水與黃河故道的船運。金軍這邊，靠城頭的弓弩、檑木、挑堮與火藥砲（宋金以來已見於太原、樊城之戰的霹靂砲），以及在城內挖地道對掘以截斷蒙古的地道。圍城四個月，金軍的器械大致完好，卻先耗盡了軍糧——這一場城下的勝負，是配重投石車與糧秣工程學共同決定的。
kitsEn: The card shows a counterweight trebuchet of the European type current around 1100: a long arm with a box of stone or packed earth slung at its short end, throwing the missile over the wall on the leverage of the weight. Its range ran to several hundred paces, far beyond that of any bow, so it could shoot into the city over the ramparts and strike men and machines behind the wall; the price was bulk, slow loading and poor accuracy, and it demanded a levelled base, taut ropes and a full crew of men, so once the position was pressed or raided it could hardly be moved. The Chinese counterpart of the same period was the traction trebuchet worked by human levers, the paoche: simple to build and easy to shift, but weaker in range and power than a machine weighted by a fall. The great counterweight guns reached China from the west in the late twelfth and early thirteenth centuries; the first name the Yuan History gives them is the Huihui pao of the siege of Caizhou in 1234, whose stones are recorded as weighing over a hundred jin and whose report was like thunder. By the siege of Bianjing in 1232 the assault train already carried western-region artillerists and enormous stone engines, and the Jin and Yuan narratives of the siege use the words for tunnelling and for throwing stones. The train also included battering rams, folding ladders, siege towers, planks and brushwood for filling the ditch, and it sealed the water route on the Bian canal and the old course of the Yellow River. The Jin replied from the walls with bows and crossbows, logs and poles, and gunpowder artillery of the kind the Song and Jin had already used at Taiyuan and Fancheng; they also dug counter-tunnels inside the city to cut off the Mongols' sappers. Four months into the siege the Jin's equipment was largely intact while their grain was gone, and the decision taken beneath the walls of Bianjing was made by a counterweight trebuchet and by the logistics of food together.
tactics: 蒙古的戰法可以拆成三步。第一步是割援：不急著攻堅城，先在唐、鄧一線游弋，等金國十五萬援軍離開營盤、在雪野行軍中疲憊，再以大軍邀擊於鈞州三峰山。這是汴京之戰的前提——金廷把希望全押在援軍上，援軍一沒，攻城就變成拖時間。第二步是合圍與封鎖：拖雷部自西北、速不台部自北面抵達，會師後四面合圍，環城掘壕，壕溝寬處以板橋、柴土與沙袋填平以通步卒；沿汴水與黃河故道斷絕水陸援道，分兵監視各城門與地道口，割斷內外消息往來。第三步是攻堅三法：其一，配重投石車架在城外預設砲位，先打女牆與城樓，壓住守軍射界，逼守軍縮在牆下；其二，穴地掘進，把進攻引入地下，金軍亦在城內挖地道對掘，兩條地道在土中相遇便展開貼身相搏；其三，飛梯、撞車與正面突擊配合使用，梯子靠牆即遭檑木，撞車撞門即被城頭火砲與挑堮擊毀。蒙古軍並不急於強攻，圍城以月計，糧盡比牆破更早到來，時間本身就是攻城武器。金軍的守法也自有章法：內城與外城（羅城）兩重城垣構成縱深，甕城與城樓提供交叉火力，弓弩手居高壓制，壕溝與拒馬阻止填壕的蒙古步卒接近牆根，並出城小隊夜襲蒙古砲位與攻城器械。
tacticsEn: The Mongol method breaks into three steps. The first was to cut off the relief: rather than hurry against a fortress, they stayed in the neighbourhood of Tangzhou and Dengzhou until the Jin host of 150,000 had left its camp and was worn out on the march through the snow, and then brought the main body against it at Mount Three Peaks near Jinzhou. This was the precondition of the siege of Bianjing, because the Jin court had staked everything on the relief army, and once that army was gone the siege became a matter of time. The second step was to encircle and seal: Tolui arrived from the north-west and Subutai from the north, and after they joined hands the city was surrounded on all four sides, a ditch dug around it and the wider places bridged over with planks, brushwood and sacks of earth so that infantry could cross. The water route on the Bian canal and the old Yellow River channel was closed, and detachments watched the gates and the mouths of the tunnels, cutting the city off from any news. The third step was the three methods of assault. First, counterweight trebuchets were set up on prepared emplacements outside the walls to batter the parapets and towers, pinning the defenders' shooting arcs and forcing them to duck behind the merlons. Second, the sappers tunnelled forward, taking the assault underground, while the Jin drove counter-tunnels from inside to meet them, and the two galleries met in the soil in a fight fought at arm's length in the dark. Third, ladders, battering rams and a frontal push were used together, and every ladder that touched the wall met a rolling log while every ram was broken by gunpowder and poles from above. The Mongols were in no hurry to storm the place: the siege was counted in months, hunger came to the wall before the wall came down, and time itself was a siege engine. The Jin defence was disciplined in its own way. The inner city and the outer wall made two lines of depth, the barbicans and towers gave crossing fire, archers and crossbowmen fired from above, the ditch and chevaux-de-frise kept the Mongols' sappers off the foot of the wall, and small parties sallied out by night to wreck the artillery positions and the siege engines.
data: 可以核對的數字有幾組。時間上，一二三二年正月蒙古大軍合圍汴京，四月城破，圍城約四個月；同年二月蒙古軍已打下洛陽，其後河北、河南、山西州縣望風而降。援軍方面，金國北援十五萬人，其中騎兵二萬、步兵十三萬，見於《金史·完顏合達傳》，這一軍在三峰山盡沒，是汴京最直接的戰前數字。守城方面，汴京分內城與外城（羅城）兩重，外城之外有引黃河故道與汴水而成的護城河，據金廷方面的記載，城內可用軍士約四萬，另有壯丁二萬可充守備與轉運；城破之後，留在城中的軍械、攻城器械與大批糧秣多被蒙古軍拆取，數字已無從核對。時間點上，一二三二年四月哀宗出奔歸德，一二三三年遷蔡州，一二三四年正月宋蒙聯軍破蔡州，金朝告終；蒙古軍追擊哀宗時分路搜索，中原各州縣多不戰而降。配重式投石機的技術錨點是：歐洲十二世紀初已有明確的配重式攻城砲記載，一二三二年汴京城下所用石砲的規模已遠非人力拋石可比；至一二三四年蔡州，《元史》記回回砲所發石彈重逾百斤，響如雷霆，中者立潰。氣候與地形同樣有記錄：圍城自冬末起，三峰山時值暴雪，汴京一帶壕溝泥濘、河面未開，填壕與架砲都吃了天氣的虧；冬日黃河故道水量小，封鎖船運反而容易。
dataEn: Several groups of figures can be checked. In time: the Mongols closed around Bianjing in the first month of 1232 and the city fell in the fourth month, a siege of about four months; in the second month the Mongols had already taken Luoyang, and after that the prefectures of Hebei, Henan and Shanxi came down without a battle. On the relief: the Jin host of 150,000, with 20,000 cavalry and 130,000 infantry, is recorded in the History of Jin in the biography of Wanyan Heda, and it was this army that was destroyed at Mount Three Peaks, the most immediate pre-siege figure of all. On the defence: Bianjing had an inner city and an outer city, and outside the latter lay a moat fed by the old course of the Yellow River and by the Bian canal; according to the Jin court's own figures some 40,000 soldiers remained inside, with 20,000 able-bodied men for guard and transport work. When the city fell, the ordnance, the siege engines, the siege material and a great quantity of grain left behind were stripped by the Mongols, and no tally of them survives. On dates: in the fourth month of 1232 Aizong fled to Guide; in 1233 the court moved to Caizhou; in the first month of 1234 the Song and Mongol allies took Caizhou and the Jin ended. The Mongols pursued in several columns, searching the country for the emperor, and the prefectures of the Central Plain came over without a fight. The technical anchor for the machine on the card is this: counterweight siege engines appear in European records at the beginning of the twelfth century, and the stone throwers used before Bianjing in 1232 were of a scale that human traction could never match; by Caizhou in 1234 the Yuan History records that the Huihui pao sent stones weighing over a hundred jin with a report like thunder, and whatever they struck was smashed at once. Weather and ground are recorded too: the siege began at the end of the winter, Mount Three Peaks was fought in a blizzard, and around Bianjing the ditches were mud and the river was still frozen, which cost both the sappers and the artillery more than the engineers could make up; in winter the old Yellow River carried little water, and closing the water route was correspondingly easy.
cause: 起因分遠近。遠因是第一次蒙古伐金留下的爛帳：一二一三至一二一五年蒙古軍攻陷中都，一二一四年金宣宗把都城遷到汴京，把中原最稠密的財賦、人丁與漕運樞紐拱手交出，河南從此成了蒙古南下中原與西征的跳板。成吉思汗臨終遺計也把這座城寫進去：金兵精銳屯潼關，南據連山、北限黃河，難以遽破，若假道於宋，宋金世仇必許，則可下兵唐、鄧、直搗大梁，金急必徵兵潼關，援兵千里赴援，人馬疲弊，雖至弗能戰，破之必矣——拖雷在一二三一年強行執行了這套計畫。直接導火線是一二三一年拖雷破大散關、鳳州，繞道漢水取唐、鄧，一二三二年正月兵臨城下；此前蒙古遣使議和被金將移剌蒲阿扣押，金朝還聲言已備軍馬可戰，兩國從此再無轉圜。金廷自身的困局同樣致命：潼關、陝西盡失，財政與兵源靠臨時括取，十五萬大軍是紙面數字，援軍被殲之後，汴京只剩四面牆和一座快要空的糧倉。結構性的原因則在蒙古軍的本質：它是不需要長期佔領每一座城池、只需拖垮對方、切斷補給的野戰與工程型軍隊，圍城數月而城自潰，正是這種戰法的典型產物。
causeEn: The causes are both distant and immediate. The distant one is the wreckage left by the first Mongol invasion of Jin: between 1213 and 1215 the Mongols took Zhongdu, and in 1214 Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bianjing, handing over the densest concentrations of wealth, population and canal transport in the Central Plain, so that Henan became the springboard for Mongol campaigning into China and into the west. Genghis Khan's plan on his deathbed named that city as well: the Jin's best troops sat behind Tong Pass, holding the mountain chain to the south and the Yellow River to the north, and could not be broken in a hurry; but if the Mongols borrowed the road through Song, and Song and Jin were old enemies, the Song would surely agree, and the army could then move down through Tang and Deng and strike straight at Daliang, and Jin, in alarm, would have to call up troops from Tong Pass, who would cover a thousand li, arrive exhausted, and be unable to fight, and would therefore be certain to be beaten. Tolui forced that plan through in 1231. The immediate spark was the breaching of Dasan Pass and Fengzhou, the march down the Han River to seize Tang and Deng, and the appearance of the army before the city in the first month of 1232; before that, Mongol envoys sent to negotiate had been detained by the Jin general Yelü Pua, and the Jin court had boasted that its horses were ready and could come and fight, after which there was no turning back for either side. The Jin's own predicament was no less fatal: with Tong Pass and Shaanxi lost, revenue and manpower depended on hurried levies, the 150,000 men were a paper figure, and once the relief army was destroyed Bianjing was left with four walls and a granary that was nearly empty. The structural reason lies in the nature of the Mongol army: it was a field and engineering army that needed not to hold every city it took, only to wear out the enemy and cut its supplies, and a city that surrendered after months of siege was the standard product of that way of war.
impact: 汴京陷落是金朝由崩潰走向覆滅的轉折。城破之後，金國失去首都與河南的財賦，河北、河南、山西的州縣多不戰而降，哀宗一路南逃歸德、蔡州，一二三四年正月蔡州城破時自盡，金朝在中原的統治終結。裝備與人力的損失更難補：守城的重裝、弓弩、火藥與反攻城具隨城破大量流入蒙古軍隊，而金廷再也重建不出一支能守的城防軍，只能靠收攏潰兵與括取的鄉兵苟延。蒙古方面，汴梁與河南的糧源、人力與工料使窩闊台得以在一二三二年同時推動第二次西征，拔都與速不台率軍西進；一二三四年之後，蒙古在華北的統治與漢地州縣、屯田、括戶之制成為長題。對南宋，這是一個警告與機遇：蒙古打通華北的通道後，一二三三年孟珙收復襄陽、樊城，一二三四年宋蒙聯軍破蔡州，宋廷收回了部分故地，卻也從此面對一個統一北方的強敵，襄樊與釣魚城的攻防成為下一階段的焦點，直至一二六七年襄樊、一二七九年崖山。技術層面上，汴京與蔡州兩役把配重式巨砲在中國的使用推到記錄可查的高峰，也留給後人一個反面教材：守方若只剩城牆而無糧、無援、無退路，工程學比任何一次衝鋒都更致命。
impactEn: The fall of Bianjing turned the Jin from a state in collapse into a state destroyed. With the capital and the wealth of Henan gone, the prefectures of Hebei, Henan and Shanxi came over without a battle, Aizong fled south to Guide and then to Caizhou, and in the first month of 1234 he killed himself when Caizhou fell, ending Jin rule in the Central Plain. The loss of men and equipment was harder to repair: the heavy armour, the bows and crossbows, the gunpowder stores and the anti-siege tools of the garrison passed into Mongol hands in bulk, and the Jin court could no longer raise a garrison army worth the name, and could only survive on stragglers gathered up and on levies taken by force. For the Mongols, the grain, the men and the craft of Bianjing and Henan allowed Ogedei to push the second western campaign at the same time, Batu and Subutai marching into Europe; after 1234 the governance of North China, with its prefectures, its colonies of settlers and its registrations of households, became a long problem. For the Southern Song this was both warning and opportunity: with the Mongols holding the passes into the north, Meng Gong recovered Xiangyang and Fancheng in 1233, and in 1234 the Song-Mongol alliance took Caizhou, so the Song recovered part of the old country and at the same time found itself facing a power master of the north, with the sieges of Xiangyang and Diaoyu Castle to come, and finally the campaign of 1267 at Xiangyang and the battle of Yamen in 1279. At the level of technology, the sieges of Bianjing and Caizhou carried the use of the great counterweight gun in China as high as the records will show, and they left behind a lesson: a defending side that has nothing but a wall, with no grain, no relief and no way out, is destroyed by engineering far more surely than by any charge.
result: 結局是金國的京城失守、主力耗盡。一二三二年正月蒙古東路與河北方向之師會師，四面包圍汴京；正月之內，十五萬北援大軍在鈞州三峰山被全殲，援兵之路自此斷絕；二月，蒙古軍打下洛陽；三月起圍城愈緊，投石砲壓住城頭，穴地掘進逼近城根，金廷屢遣使出城求援議和皆無回音。到四月，城中軍糧告罄，守軍器械尚存而人已不支，完顏合剌等人自盡殉城，汴京陷落。金哀宗完顏守緒與諸王、大臣出奔歸德，蒙古軍入城後拆取城中的砲車、攻城器材、糧秣與軍械，中原州縣隨之望風而降。蒙古軍分路追擊，一二三三年占據歸德與河南大部，金哀宗再遷蔡州，一二三四年正月宋蒙聯軍攻破蔡州，金朝滅亡。戰略結果可以這樣總結：蒙古以工程與封鎖代替強攻，用四個月的時間換來一座空城，再以空城震懾整個中原；金國失去了最後的戰爭縱深，也失去了重建的可能。對整個東亞，此役把守城必待援這個信念徹底打破——三峰山的援軍被殲，汴京即告崩潰；四年後蔡州再無援軍，金朝便真的滅亡了。
resultEn: The result was the loss of the Jin capital and the exhaustion of the field army. In the first month of 1232 the eastern column and the column coming down from Hebei joined hands and surrounded Bianjing; within that same month the relief host of 150,000 was annihilated at Mount Three Peaks near Jinzhou and the road of help was cut for good; in the second month the Mongols took Luoyang; from the third month the siege tightened, the stone throwers pressed down on the walls and the sappers came up under them, and the envoys the court sent out again and again for help and for terms met with nothing. In the fourth month the grain of the garrison was spent, the equipment was still there but the men were not, Wanyan Hela and others killed themselves rather than surrender, and Bianjing fell. Aizong fled to Guide with his princes and ministers; the Mongols stripped the city of its guns, siege engines, grain and ordnance; and the prefectures of the Central Plain came down without a fight. The Mongols pursued in several columns, took Guide and most of Henan in 1233, and Aizong moved once more to Caizhou, where in the first month of 1234 the Song and Mongol allies stormed the city and the Jin was extinguished. In strategic terms the summary is this: the Mongols substituted engineering and blockade for assault, spent four months to take an empty city, and then used that empty city to terrify the whole Central Plain, while the Jin lost its last depth of defence and with it any possibility of recovery. For East Asia as a whole the battle demolished the belief that a walled city must wait for relief: the relief army was destroyed at Mount Three Peaks and Bianjing began to crumble; four years later Caizhou had no relief at all, and the Jin truly died.
